description: Litmus helps  SREs and developers practice chaos engineering in a Cloud-native way. Chaos experiments are published at the ChaosHub  (https://hub.litmuschaos.io). Community notes is at https://hackmd.io/a4Zu_sH4TZGeih-xCimi3Q

summary.one_liner: LitmusChaos is an open source, CNCF-hosted chaos engineering platform that runs and monitors fault-injection experiments on Kubernetes using custom resources.
summary.what_it_does: The platform runs as a set of microservices and defines chaos intent and steady-state hypotheses through Kubernetes custom resources. ChaosExperiment resources are installable templates that describe the fault library, required permissions, and default settings, and they allow third-party fault-injection tools to be plugged in (BYOC). ChaosEngine resources link an application workload, node, or infrastructure component to a fault, with run tuning and 'probes' for steady-state validation. ChaosResult resources hold per-validation outcomes, fault revert status, and a verdict, and a chaos-exporter exposes results as Prometheus metrics. Experiments can be grouped into Workflows that run in a chosen order, and a centralized chaos-center component is used to construct, schedule, and visualize them. Shared experiments are published on ChaosHub (hub.litmuschaos.io).
use_cases: Running chaos tests during application development alongside unit or integration tests
Adding fault injection as a stage in CI/CD pipelines
Scheduling chaos experiments against Kubernetes workloads and infrastructure
Collecting chaos experiment results as Prometheus metrics
Finding and sharing reusable chaos experiments via ChaosHub
how_to_run: Read the Litmus Docs Getting Started section and follow the Installation instructions
No specific install or run commands are given in the README
stack: Argo Workflows (named in a related video title only)
notable: Uses Kubernetes CRDs (ChaosExperiment, ChaosEngine, ChaosResult, Workflow) to define and track chaos runs
BYOC support lets experiments wrap third-party fault-injection tooling
ChaosHub public library where vendors and developers share experiments
Chaos-exporter publishes experiment verdicts as Prometheus metrics
caveats: Targets Kubernetes environments; the README describes no non-Kubernetes use
Setup details are deferred to external Litmus Docs rather than the README
Multi-component architecture (chaos-center, chaos agent, operators) implies a non-trivial installation
